issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit: the template class defines __init__(self, num_qubits: int) (expects a parameter) while the solution and the class usage assume a no-argument constructor (__init__(self)). This inconsistency will confuse students about how to instantiate the class and where to supply the number of qubits.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template constructor match the intended no-argument design used in the solution and run() examples. Change the template __init__ signature to def __init__(self): (and keep number_of_qubits_query_register as a filled value inside) or, if a parameter is intended, update the solution and run() usage and the problem statement to require passing num_qubits when instantiating the class.

issues.description: Return-type inconsistency for GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit.simulate: the problem statement and exercise text request returning the 'statevector' (an object/vector), the template annotates the method to return list[complex], but the solution returns the object from result.get_statevector (a Statevector/array). This mismatch between the template annotation and the actual expected/solution return type may confuse students about the expected type to return.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template's simulate() type annotation with the intended return value: either change the template annotation to return the same Statevector type (or a more general 'Any'/'Statevector'/'np.ndarray') or update the solution to return a plain list[complex]. Also document in the exercise whether a Qiskit Statevector object or a raw complex array is expected.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit: the template defines __init__(self, num_qubits: int) while the solution and the typical usage in the repository call the class with no arguments (solution uses __init__(self) and run() in the template/README examples instantiate GroverTwoQubitWithoutAuxiliaryQubit() with no parameter). This inconsistent constructor parameter naming/usage creates confusion for students about how to initialize the class and will likely cause a runtime error or extra cognitive load resolving which signature is correct.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template constructor signature match the solution and typical usage. Change the template __init__ to def __init__(self): (remove the num_qubits parameter) and set self.number_of_qubits_query_register = 2 in the template, mirroring the solution. Alternatively, if the intent is to allow a num_qubits parameter, update the solution and all instantiations to accept and propagate that parameter consistently.
